en.title: Stress in Verb Endings
en.summary: Learn how to place the main stress on the final syllable of Romanian verb endings correctly.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: Many Romanian action words put the stress at the very end. You hear the last beat ring out clearly. Listen to (vorbiți) /vorˈbit͡s/, which means you speak. The voice pushes hard on the final part. Hear it also in (citiți) /t͡ʃiˈtit͡s/, which means you read. The ending carries the loudest punch.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Start soft and save your energy for the end. Open your mouth wide for the final vowel sound. Give that final beat more time and volume. Make your pitch jump up slightly at the end. Do not rush past the word ending. Drop your energy only after you finish the word.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Look closely at the word endings in written text. Endings often hold the main stress in these forms. When you see (mâncați) /mɨnˈkat͡s/, which means you eat, hit the end. The letters at the start stay short and light. Always direct your voice toward the final vowel. The strongest sound sits right there.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not stress the first syllable of the word. Many learners pull the stress forward by mistake. Never let the ending become quiet or weak. Keep the ending clear, loud, and proud. If you weaken the ending, people may misunderstand you. Always land firmly on that last beat.
